# GitForge — Full site content

> GitForge is a free, MIT-licensed desktop Git client for macOS, Windows, and Linux with a graph-first interface — commit graph, branch sidebar, working tree, multi-repo tabs, and real local Git operations via the native Git CLI. No account or subscription is required.

Version: 1.0.2 · License: MIT · Author: gitforge · Stack: Wails 3 (Go), Vue 3, TypeScript, Pinia, Tailwind CSS 4

Website: https://jh12ops.github.io/GitForge/
Repository: https://github.com/JH12Ops/GitForge
Download: https://github.com/JH12Ops/GitForge/releases

---

## Overview

GitForge is a desktop Git client with a graph-first interface. It provides a three-pane repository view that runs real Git commands against local repositories via typed HTTP gateway commands to a pure Go backend. Open a folder, clone from a URL, start a repo with init, browse history, manage branches, stage files, commit, fetch/pull/push, and inspect diffs.

GitForge is a Wails 3 app. The renderer never shells out to Git directly — the Go backend runs the native `git` CLI and exposes typed gateway commands to the Vue 3 renderer.

## Features

### Clone, init & discovery
Clone from a URL with progress and cancel, start a repo with init, or scan a folder to find nested repositories. Opening a subfolder resolves to the repo root. No account required.

### Commit graph
Virtualized SVG lanes with a pending-changes row, infinite scroll, and arrow-key selection across history.

### Branch sidebar
Favorites, remotes, tags, stashes, and worktrees — drag branches to merge or rebase.

### Working tree
Flat or tree file list, per-hunk staging, conflict resolution, and commit composition. File type icons per path.

### Diff viewer
Unified/split modes, syntax highlighting, per-hunk staging, blame overlay with file history, and word wrap. Binary images render side-by-side with zoom, pan, and a fullscreen lightbox.

### Interactive rebase
Reorder, squash, fixup, drop, or edit commits in a dialog before starting the rebase.

### Multi-repo tabs
Open several repositories at once — switch between tabs and pick up where you left off. Reopen the last closed tab, cycle with keyboard, or jump to a tab by index.

### Blame & file history
Inline blame overlay with author blocks, per-revision file history, and optional word wrap for long lines.

### Remote sync + auto-fetch
Fetch, pull, push, and sync from the toolbar — with ahead/behind counts in the status bar. Optional background auto-fetch on a configurable interval.

### Search & shortcuts
Search commits and files by message or path (non-matching graph rows dim). Navigate history and drive the UI from the keyboard — every shortcut is remappable in Settings → Shortcuts with conflict detection.

### Git output log
Per-tab drawer listing each executed git command with stdout/stderr and ok/error status. Clear per tab.

### Auto-update checks
Packaged builds compare against GitHub Releases on startup. Check manually anytime from the app menu.

### Real Git backend
Native `git` CLI in the Go backend via typed gateway commands — mock mode available for UI-only dev.

### Credits & attribution
Settings credits panel with project links and open-source licenses. Native About dialog on all platforms.

### System terminal
Open the OS terminal at the repo root with ⌘T.

### Themes & UI mode
Default, Dracula, Light, Claude, or System appearance. Basic mode hides advanced actions for a simpler toolbar.

### Polished layout
Collapsible sidebars with expand rails, resizable panes, and commit graph zoom for dense history views.

## Feature status matrix

| Area | Status |
|------|--------|
| Real Git backend (`git` CLI in Go backend; renderer never shells out) | Supported |
| Open local repos · recent repos · multi-repo tabs (reopen closed, cycle, jump-to-index) · startup screen | Supported |
| Commit graph — lanes, refs, pagination, shift-compare, keyboard nav, search dimming | Supported |
| Branch sidebar — favorites, tags, stashes, worktrees; drag-and-drop merge/rebase; section context menus | Supported |
| Working tree — flat/tree view, stage/unstage (patch hunks), commit, file type icons | Supported |
| Diff viewer — unified/split, syntax highlighting, per-hunk staging, blame overlay with file history, word wrap · image diffs (zoom, pan, lightbox) | Supported |
| Fetch / pull / push / sync · remote maintenance (fetch all, prune, push tags) · auto-fetch interval | Supported |
| Merge / rebase / interactive rebase / cherry-pick (continue/abort banner) | Supported |
| Merge conflict resolution (ours/theirs/per-block) | Supported |
| Undo / redo (reflog-backed) · stash · search | Supported |
| Git output log — per-tab executed commands with stdout/stderr | Supported |
| Command palette (⌘K) · customizable keyboard shortcuts (remappable, conflict detection) | Supported |
| Open system terminal at the repo root (⌘T toolbar action) | Supported |
| Themes — Default, Dracula, Light, Claude, System (settings) | Supported |
| Collapsible sidebars with expand rails · commit graph zoom | Supported |
| UI mode — Basic (essential actions) or Advanced (full toolbar and sidebar) | Supported |
| Open on GitHub · app preferences (appearance, layout, graph, sidebar, sync/auto-fetch, shortcuts, credits) | Supported |
| Credits & attribution (settings panel + native About dialog) | Supported |
| Resizable three-pane layout · file watcher auto-refresh | Supported |
| Auto-update check (packaged builds) · Check for Updates… menu | Supported |
| Clone (URL, progress + cancel) · init new repository · folder discovery | Supported |
| Hosting auth UI (OAuth sign-in, private-host browsing) | Not yet |

## Tech stack

Wails 3 (Go), Vue 3, TypeScript, Pinia, reka-ui, Tailwind CSS 4, Vitest, Vite.

## Download & install

Download the latest installer from GitHub Releases:
- macOS: `.app.zip` (Apple silicon + Intel) — unzip and drag GitForge to Applications

Use **GitForge → Check for Updates…** to check for new versions in packaged builds.

### Build from source

```
git clone https://github.com/JH12Ops/GitForge.git
cd gitforge
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Frequently asked questions

### What is GitForge?
GitForge is a free, open-source desktop Git client for macOS, Windows, and Linux. It shows a commit graph, branch sidebar, and working tree in a resizable three-pane layout, running real `git` commands against your local repositories.

### Is GitForge free?
Yes. GitForge is MIT-licensed and free to download and use.

### What platforms does GitForge support?
Packaged builds are available for macOS (.app.zip, Apple silicon + Intel) on GitHub Releases. Developers can build and run it locally on macOS with Node.js, npm, and Go.

### Does GitForge require an account?
No sign-in, cloud sync, or subscription. Open a local folder, clone from a URL, or start a new repo and work with your Git repositories offline.

### How is GitForge different from GitKraken or Sourcetree?
GitForge is a lightweight, open-source alternative focused on a fast commit graph and direct Git CLI operations — without vendor accounts or lock-in. Built with Wails 3, Vue 3, TypeScript, and a pure Go backend.
